questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following cations gives a chocolate brown precipitate upon addition of aqueous solution of $K_4[Fe(CN)_6]$?
questions.solution:
Reaction of $Cu^{2+}$ with potassium ferrocyanide, $K_4[Fe(CN)_6]$, yields a chocolate brown precipitate of cupric ferrocyanide.

$2Cu^{2+} + K_4[Fe(CN)_6] \rightarrow Cu_2[Fe(CN)_6] \downarrow + 4K^+$

The other ions give different coloured precipitates with $K_4[Fe(CN)_6]$:
$Fe^{3+}$ gives a Prussian blue precipitate of $Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3$.
$Zn^{2+}$ gives a white precipitate of $Zn_2[Fe(CN)_6]$.
$Ca^{2+}$ gives a white precipitate of $CaK_2[Fe(CN)_6]$.

Answer: $Cu^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is least thermally stable?
questions.solution: BeCO, is least thermally stable. The thermal stability of carbonates increases down the group i.e from Be to Ba. $\mathrm{BeCO}_{3} < \mathrm{MgCO}_{3} < \mathrm{CaCO}_{3} < \mathrm{SrCO}_{3} < \mathrm{BaCO}_{3}(523 \mathrm{K}) \quad(813 \mathrm{K})(1173 \mathrm{K}) \quad(1562 \mathrm{K}) \quad(1633 \mathrm{K})$ BeCO, is unstable to the extent that it is stable only in atmosphere of $\mathrm{CO}_{y}$. These carbonates show reversible decomposition in closed container. $M \mathrm{CO}, \quad \rightarrow \mathrm{MO}+\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ More stable the oxide is formed, lesser will be stability of carbonates.

questions.q: Which of the following arrangements is correct in respect of solubility in water?
questions.solution: The correct order of solubility of sulphates in water is $\mathrm{BeSO}_{4} > \mathrm{MgSO}_{4} > \mathrm{CaSO}_{4} > \mathrm{SrSO}_{4} > $$\mathrm{BaSO}_{4}$$ Solublity of 2nd group sulphates decreases as we down the group due to less release of hydration energy. $$\mathrm{Be}^{2+}$ < $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$ < $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ < $\mathrm{Sr}^{2+}$ < $\mathrm{Ba}^{24}$ (lonic Size) As hydration energy decreases more rapidly than latice energy, the solubility decreases down the group. Hydration Energy $=\frac{\text{ Charge }}{\text{ Size }}$ While lathice energy almost remains constant. Hence, solubility decreases.

questions.q:
Match the flame colours of the alkaline earth metal salts in the Bunsen burner
$

A. Caicium$		p. Brick red

B. Strontium		q. Apple green

C. Barium		r. Crimson
questions.solution:
Flame colours are produced from the movement of the electrons in the metal ions present in the compounds.
Calcium gives brick red colour. Strontium gives crimson colour. Barium gives apple green colour.
